question: A car travels 128 km in the first hour and 146 km in the second hour. What is the average speed (in km / hr ) of the car for the whole journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 128 + 146 = 274 km

Total time = 2 hours

Average speed = 274 ÷ 2 = 137 km/hr

**∴ Answer = 137 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance in 1st hour = 128 km

Distance in 2nd hour = 146 km

Total time = 2 hours

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance = 128 + 146 = 274 km

⇒ Total time = 2 hours

⇒ Average speed = 274 ÷ 2

⇒ = 137 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 137 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

Equal Time Case

When time intervals are equal, average speed = (sum of distances) ÷ total time

Key Insight

Since each segment is 1 hour, just take mean of distances

Quick Tip

If time is equal, average speed = arithmetic mean of speeds
